judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the "Fale com a Ouvidoria" tile (href ESOU/HomeVisitante). The four image links in the first h2 of the content all carry aria-label="Link sem descrição", which overrides their images' alternatives: Chromium's tree (CDP) gives each link the name "Link sem descrição", nameFrom aria-label, and gives the h2 the name of four copies of it. None has a title or aria-describedby, and all four sit in the same h2 (their sentence, block and preceding heading at once), so nothing in the rubric's context list tells them apart: they form one R1 set. They lead to four non-equivalent resources (the ESOU manifestation form, the FAQ page, the statistics page and the Balcão Virtual meeting app), and the tiles visibly read "Fale com a Ouvidoria", "Perguntas mais Frequentes", "Estatísticas" and "Balcão Virtual" in the screenshot, so each link of the set fails 2.4.4 by R1; the shared name is also a placeholder that describes no purpose. I looked for a way out: the alternatives exist in the DOM and as image children in the tree, but the link's name is the aria-label, and that is what screen readers announce for the link. The live HTML still has the four aria-labels (the two internal hrefs are now absolute portaltj.tjrj.jus.br addresses, which changes nothing). The claim names this failure.

judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: The first case-number textbox in the header ("Num. única"). Its <label for> is display:none (class d-none), and Chromium's tree (CDP) gives it the name "" with a labelledby relation to that hidden label, so the claim is true of the capture. But the input also has title="Informe Primeira parte da numeração do processo" and placeholder "Num. única": HTML-AAM lists the title, then the placeholder, as fallbacks when the label yields no text, H65 (title) is a sufficient technique for naming a control, and engines that follow that fallback (and axe's name computation) name it from the title. Whether users receive a name thus depends on the browser (none in Chromium, the title elsewhere), and competent auditors would disagree whether a title that the spec makes the name, but Chromium drops, meets 4.1.2. The live HTML has the same hidden label and attributes.
